title: Potable Water Tank Capacity Increase to 200 Litres for Long-Sector ZEPHYR-24 Operations
abstract: A larger potable water tank and a re-routed distribution line for ZEPHYR-24 aircraft flying transatlantic sectors, ending the practice of carrying bottled water to make up the shortfall on long rotations.

sections.reason: Operators putting ZEPHYR-24 aircraft onto six and seven hour sectors found the 130 litre potable water capacity insufficient for a full cabin with three lavatories and two galleys in service. The practical answer in the field was to load bottled water, which costs weight, cabin stowage and crew time, and several operators reported having to restrict hot beverage service in the last hour. The tank itself was sized for the original short-haul mission and had never been revisited for the long-range variants.
sections.description: The tank is replaced by a 200 litre item carried on the existing seat track cover interface D3810110221920 with two additional cradle straps into the frame. The obsolete galley insert HOL892964-82 in the adjacent stowage is deleted to release the volume, the distribution panel KAE623945-06 is renewed with a larger bore feed to the aft galley, and tension head bolts EN594454-01 secure the extended cradle. The distribution latch FIN 17WM and the trim FIN 299WM are re-positioned by the deeper tank, and the potable water trim FIN 794WM is deleted. Work is done from zones 951, 971 and 181 with the aft lavatory and the mid galley partially stripped. Drawings D38101185882 issue C and D38101229613 issue D carry the tank envelope and the revised line routing.
sections.effects: Dry mass increase of 9.4 kg per aircraft, but the filled aircraft carries up to 70 kg more water, all of it aft, which the loading manual reflects as a revised water quantity table rather than as a fixed centre-of-gravity shift. Electrical load is unchanged. The tank is not interchangeable with the 130 litre item because the cradle interface differs. Service water quantity indication had to be recalibrated and the water servicing task times increased. AMM and IPC content for ATA 38-10 was re-issued and the drain and disinfection procedure was extended for the larger volume.
sections.embodiment_note: Cut in on the production line at MSN Z10389 in September 2020. Retrofit is a three-day activity with the aft cabin partially stripped, and is normally combined with a cabin refresh or a scheduled potable water system disinfection.

type_data.balance_impact: Aft installation; revised water quantity table issued with the loading manual
type_data.production_impact: Cut-in at MSN Z10389, absorbed in the aft cabin installation station

title: Potable Water Tank Capacity Increase to 200 Litres for Long-Sector ZEPHYR-24 Operations

issue.reason: The combined weight and balance case with the Cabin-Flex rear galley conversion is recorded and published as a loading condition.

abstract: A larger potable water tank and a re-routed distribution line for long-sector ZEPHYR-24 operations, now carrying the combined loading condition that applies when the aircraft also has the rear galley conversion.
